sources: For most of history marriage was an economic and political arrangement between families; the 'love match' ideal spread in Western Europe and America from the late 18th century, about 200 years ago. Stephanie Coontz (2005), Marriage, a History: From Obedience to Intimacy (Viking); interviews (VOA 2005; Against the Current).
About 80% of both sexes (US) say they are looking for a soulmate: Coontz interview, Against the Current. 1743 = Hogarth's 'Marriage A-la-Mode' (illustrative).

Hogarth, 'Marriage A-la-Mode: 1, The Marriage Settlement' (c. 1743, National Gallery London): the gouty earl points to his family tree, the merchant father holds the contract, the couple turn away from each other. Film: 'Charity Ball' (Edison, 1897), public domain, illustrative (Internet Archive).
